comments.comment_body: See how I create eyelets for this MD sailors bag, same deal with CLO3D - just before I thread a pull chord, where the ringlet is created from a thickened piece of cloth that has the edge radii and thickness increased to the metal ringlets dimension(s). This is the same principle you may use for any cloth garment, or 'ringlet' placed into a curtain as it allows you to sew the element into the cloth item. You may stiffen the ringlet so it does not flex by applying strength and a new 'custom' fabric physical preset to the ring itself. Dial up the stiffness factor in the physical preset to suit your project. See tutorial link &gt&gt Download MD tutorial You may apply 'strengthen' to model elements to create a smooth fabric that retains some shape, and you may also lock that into the pattern using solidify so you may still move the cloth around. So these two functions are useful for holding shape into fixings and elements on accessories. eg: hats - where stiffness and edge treatment of fabric are key features.

comments.comment_body: Hi 903237281383 For the Auto Grading Tool it is more of an "Auto Fit" then grade. The tool does not actually "Grade" patterns, but changes the size of the existing patterns in your 2D window. The Auto Grade Tool can be great for getting a starting point when jumping between size groups. Example taking your standard Medium and Auto Grading to your Plus Size which gives you a new pattern to work from. Once the Auto Grading is applied you can use that as a starting point to build out a new pattern using the CLO grading tools You can find a video explanation for Auto Grading vs Grading HERE. post_details: Hello every time I select the CF line I want to merge, it won't let me. What have I done wrong?!

comments.comment_body: Hi 7201869670169. There could be a few reasons for this. I am putting different possibilities below -Are the CF lines sewn together? If they are not sewn together you will need to select both lines with the Edit Pattern tool First and then R-Click on one of them -All of your patter outlines are Red. Have you applied Internal lines? If you have you may need to remove these first and then use the above steps. Hope this helps

post_title: Is there a way to apply a substance texture to a graphic?
post_details: Hi, I am working on a project in which I am using a Substance texture for the shell fabric. I am trying to replicate a sublimation print by adding a repeat graphic to the surface of the fabric, but I do not see an obvious way to apply the same Substance surface texture on the fabric, to the graphic. Is there a way to do this? I appreciate any help!

comments.comment_body: Yes you can do this. You may apply a normal map to the graphic from the property editor. However you may need to manually scale your normal,gloss, image to fit the weave scale for tiling - so that is maybe the only caveat.

post_details: Hi, New to Clo 3d and currently learning. For some reason when I try to edit seam allowance on dart I am unable to select just the dart point and it constantly selects either segment, so I cannot fix the dart cap. Is this a bug? I understand it was an issue that was fixed... I am using the latest version of Clo on Windows. Thanks!

comments.comment_body: Hi 7264682602265. When making the dart did you use the dart tool? Some of the seam allowance tools for darts will only be accessible if you used that tool.
Thanks for your reply! I created the dart with 'right click' and 'add dart'. Will it only work if I use dart tool?

That is the correct tool. Once you have added the dart with the R-click you can then add seam allowance with the Seam Allowance Tool (this can be done by marqueeing over the entire pattern or just the area that you want to add seam allowance to). Once the general seam allowance is added you can use the Seam Allowance Tool to select the Segment Point inside of the dart. This will give you the normal 6 Seam allowance Intersection options in the Property Editor as well as 2 additional Dart Cap options that will only be seen when using the R-Click Add dart feature. I have added a visual below for reference.
Thank you CLO Designers for the explanation!

post_details: after tracing my pattern a have really big mess with lines

comments.comment_body: Hi 7070582475929. It looks like you have traced out the same internal line multiple times. You can use the Edit pattern Tool to select the line, then choose from the drop down menu to delete them one at a time. When Tracing you can Use the trace tool &gt Select all of the edges you want to Trace out and either hit enter on your key board or R-Click on the Lines and choose trace. Just make sure to do this only one or you will end up with many extra Internal Lines

post_details: Can I change the color of the mesh display? Is it possible to render in a mesh display?

comments.comment_body: Hi hayu888, thank you for submitting a question. You can't render in a mesh view in CLO, but you can change the color of your mesh. You would first need to change the surface texture view in the 3D toggle menu to the mesh view (or press ALT+5) and then open the schematic render view. Now change from texture to color next to 'garment' and select your preferred color. Let us know if you have any other questions.

post_title: Edit graphics size after insertion on garment
post_details: I watched the video and read the guide but didn't understand how to do it. I would like to change the size of a graphic as for insertion, with exact measurements, even after placing it. Is there a field of measures like for insertion? I can not find it. thank you

comments.comment_body: Hi 6377681616281. You can fin d a detailed breakdown of how to edit. adjust, scale your graphics HERE. Or videos HERE and HERE. But I am adding screen shots showing how you can adjust Graphics. -Your first option to scale the graphic is what you show above. When first applying the graphic you can put in the size -If the graphic is already applied you can use the transform Graphic Tool in the 3D or 2D tool bars &gt L-click on the graphic &gt Use the gear that appears to rotate or scale the graphic. -Open the Graphics Tab in the Object Browser &gt Select your desired graphic and go to the below Property Editor &gt At the bottom there is a Transform Graphic option to enter a specific size Hope this helps!
